title: Multiple myeloma & precursors
subtitle: MGUS → smoldering → myeloma · treat on a myeloma-defining event, not on the M-spike · anti-CD38 quadruplets up front, T-cell redirection (CAR-T, bispecifics) moving to first relapse
source: Compiled from primary trial reports and consensus guidelines (IMWG; NCCN) verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: The plasma cell spectrum (IMWG 2014)
rows: M-protein <3 g/dL + clonal marrow PCs <10% + no CRAB / SLiM (or amyloidosis). Progresses ~1%/yr; IgM MGUS → WM, not myeloma
Abnormal FLC ratio + raised involved FLC, no heavy chain on IFE, PCs <10%, urine M <500 mg/24 h
M-protein ≥3 g/dL (or urine ≥500 mg/24 h) and/or PCs 10–60%, no CRAB / SLiM. ~10%/yr for the first 5 yr, then ~3%/yr, then ~1%/yr
Clonal PCs ≥10% (or biopsy-proven plasmacytoma) + ≥1 myeloma-defining event (below)
≥5% circulating PCs (IMWG 2021; was 20%) — treat as ultra-high risk
Single lesion, marrow <10% clonal (none = solitary; minimal = higher risk). RT 40–50 Gy

blocks.heading: Myeloma-defining events — any one = treat
items: C — Ca >11 mg/dL or >1 mg/dL above ULN · R — CrCl <40 or Cr >2 mg/dL · A — Hb <10 g/dL or >2 below LLN · B — ≥1 lytic lesion (≥5 mm) on X-ray, CT or PET-CT
SLiM (no CRAB needed): clonal PCs ≥60% · involved:uninvolved FLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L · >1 focal lesion on MRI (≥5 mm)
Osteoporosis / compression fracture without a lytic lesion is not CRAB — image first

blocks.heading: Workup
items: SPEP + serum IFE + serum FLC — plus 24-h UPEP + urine IFE once at diagnosis
CBC, CMP (Ca, Cr, albumin), β2-microglobulin, LDH, quantitative IgG/IgA/IgM
Marrow aspirate + biopsy: PC %, flow, FISH on CD138-sorted cells — t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), t(11;14), del(17p), 1q+, del(1p); TP53 sequencing where available
Whole-body low-dose CT or PET-CT; whole-body MRI if SMM with a negative CT/PET. Skeletal survey is obsolete (insensitive)
Albuminuria or unexplained organ dysfunction → think AL amyloidosis (fat pad, NT-proBNP, troponin)
Type & screen with extended RBC phenotype/genotype before the first anti-CD38 dose (page 3)

boxes: stop dara at ≥24 mo if CR + MRD-neg ≥12 mo
len alone if no dara induction / not tolerated

blocks.heading: Smoldering myeloma — who to treat
items: Mayo 2/20/20: M-protein >2 g/dL, marrow PCs >20%, FLC ratio >20. 0 / 1 / ≥2 factors → median time to progression 110 / 68 / 29 months
High-risk SMM → daratumumab SC ×3 yr (AQUILA vs active monitoring): PFS HR 0.49, 5-yr PFS 63% vs 41%, OS HR 0.52 — FDA 6 Nov 2025, the first approved SMM therapy
Lenalidomide (E3A06, intermediate/high risk): PFS HR 0.28; no OS signal
Low-risk SMM: observe — treating it is not supported

blocks.heading: MGUS — Mayo risk (20-yr progression)
rows: M-protein ≥1.5 g/dL · non-IgG · abnormal FLC ratio — 0 factors
blocks.footnote: Low-risk MGUS (IgG, M <1.5, normal ratio): no marrow or imaging needed; recheck at 6 mo then every 2–3 yr. Anything else: marrow + imaging, then yearly labs.

blocks.heading: Staging
rows: I: β2M <3.5 mg/L + albumin ≥3.5 g/dL · III: β2M ≥5.5 · II: neither
I: ISS I + standard-risk FISH + normal LDH · III: ISS III + high-risk FISH [del(17p), t(4;14), t(14;16)] or high LDH · II: rest. 5-yr OS 82 / 62 / 40%
Points: ISS III 1.5, ISS II 1, del(17p) 1, high LDH 1, t(4;14) 1, 1q+ 0.5 → I 0 · II 0.5–1 · III 1.5–2.5 · IV 3–5. Median OS NR / 109 / 69 / 38 mo. Splits the big R-ISS II group

blocks.heading: High-risk myeloma — IMS/IMWG 2025 (any one)
items: del(17p) in >20% cancer clonal fraction and/or TP53 mutation
IgH translocation [t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20)] + 1q gain/amp and/or del(1p32) — translocation alone no longer qualifies
Biallelic del(1p32), or monoallelic del(1p32) + 1q gain/amp
β2M ≥5.5 mg/L with normal creatinine (<1.2 mg/dL)
Also high risk in practice: plasma cell leukemia, extramedullary disease, relapse <12–18 mo from front-line therapy (functional). t(11;14), t(6;14), hyperdiploidy = standard risk

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — the evidence: newly diagnosed disease, response and MRD, relapse, T-cell redirection

blocks.heading: Newly diagnosed — the trials that set the standard
rows: D-VRd vs VRd induction/consolidation + ASCT, then D-R vs R: 6-yr PFS 81.1% vs 56.1% (HR 0.35, 81-mo update, meeting report); MRD-neg 75% vs 48%. Dara stopped after ≥24 mo if sustained MRD-neg. FDA 30 Jul 2024 for D-VRd induction + consolidation only (not D-R maintenance)
RVd ± ASCT, then len: PFS 67.5 vs 46.2 mo (IFM: 50 vs 36) — no OS difference (5-yr 80.7% vs 79.2%). ASCT buys PFS, not OS; deferral with cells banked is legitimate
Isa-KRd ×6, then MRD-guided. MRD-neg (10−5): ASCT vs 6 more Isa-KRd — MRD-neg 10−6 86% vs 84% (P=0.64). MRD+: tandem vs single ASCT 32% vs 40% (NS). MRD endpoint only, 17-mo follow-up, no PFS yet
After ASCT: PFS 52.8 vs 23.5 mo, OS HR 0.75; more second primary malignancies
MRD+ after ASCT: D-R vs R maintenance — MRD-neg conversion at 12 mo 50.5% vs 18.8%; PFS HR 0.53
DRd vs Rd until progression: median PFS NR vs 34.4 mo (HR 0.53), OS HR 0.68
VRd vs Rd: PFS 43 vs 30 mo, OS 75 vs 64 mo (HR 0.71)
D-VRd vs VRd ×8 → D-Rd vs Rd: MRD-neg 60.9% vs 39.4%; PFS HR 0.57. FDA 27 Jan 2026 (TIE only)
Isa-VRd vs VRd: 5-yr PFS 63.2% vs 45.2% (HR 0.60). FDA Sep 2024
blocks.footnote: No head-to-head quadruplet vs DRd in TIE. Quadruplets for fit older adults; DRd for intermediate-fit / frail.

blocks.heading: Fitness and dose adjustment
items: IMWG frailty score (age, Charlson, ADL, IADL; 0–5): fit 0 · intermediate 1 · frail ≥2 — 3-yr OS 84% / 76% / 57%; frail have ~2× the discontinuation rate
Age >75 or frail: dexamethasone 20 mg weekly, weekly SC bortezomib, renally dosed lenalidomide

blocks.heading: Response (IMWG 2016)
rows: CR + no clonal PCs at ≤10−5 (NGF or NGS); sustained = confirmed ≥1 yr apart; imaging MRD-neg adds PET-negative
Negative serum + urine IFE, plasmacytomas gone, <5% marrow PCs (sCR adds normal FLC ratio, no clonal PCs by IHC)
≥90% M-protein fall (or IFE+ / SPEP−) / ≥50% serum and ≥90% urine fall
≥25% rise from nadir: serum M ≥0.5 g/dL absolute, urine ≥200 mg/24 h, or dFLC >10 mg/dL; new lesions
blocks.footnote: MRD is prognostic, and now regulatory: ODAC 12–0 (Apr 2024) accepted MRD-neg CR as an accelerated-approval endpoint. CEPHEUS (Jan 2026) used MRD-neg as its primary endpoint; iberdomide (Aug 2026) = first accelerated approval of a new drug based on MRD. Stopping therapy on MRD alone is still a trial question.

blocks.heading: Relapse — by what the patient is refractory to
rows: Triple-class exposed = PI + IMiD + anti-CD38. Refractory = progression on or ≤60 days after. Penta = 2 PIs + 2 IMiDs + anti-CD38. Treat biochemical relapse early if high-risk or rapid rise
Cilta-cel (CARTITUDE-4): PFS NR vs 11.8 mo (HR 0.26), OS HR 0.55. Teclistamab + dara (MajesTEC-3): 36-mo PFS 83% vs 30% (HR 0.17), OS HR 0.46. BVd (DREAMM-7): PFS 36.6 vs 13.4 mo, OS HR 0.58

Dara-Kd (CANDOR, HR 0.63) · Isa-Kd (IKEMA, HR 0.53) · DPd (APOLLO, 12.4 vs 6.9 mo) · Isa-Pd (ICARIA, 11.5 vs 6.5 mo) · IberDd (iberdomide, Zenbexus; accelerated Aug 2026, ≥1 prior line incl PI + IMiD)
Teclistamab monotherapy (MajesTEC-9 vs PVd/Kd): PFS HR 0.29, OS HR 0.60, grade 3–4 infection 42%. BPd (DREAMM-8 vs PVd): 12-mo PFS 71% vs 51%. CAR-T
BCMA CAR-T, BCMA or GPRC5D bispecific (table below) · SVd (BOSTON: PFS 13.9 vs 9.5 mo) · clinical trial
blocks.footnote: Cilta-cel vs ide-cel: ide-cel (KarMMa-3, 2–4 prior lines) PFS 13.3 vs 4.4 mo but no OS gain (HR 1.01, 56% crossover). Both CAR-Ts show early excess deaths during manufacturing/bridging — bridge effectively.

blocks.heading: T-cell redirection and ADC — approvals
rows: BCMA · ≥1 prior line, len-refractory · OS benefit. Delayed parkinsonism, cranial-nerve palsy (9%), GBS
BCMA · ≥2 prior lines (IMiD, PI, anti-CD38) · PFS benefit, OS not shown
BCMA×CD3 SC · + dara, ≥1 line (5 Mar 2026) · mono ≥4 lines (ORR 63%) converted to regular approval 5 Mar 2026
GPRC5D×CD3 SC · ≥4 lines (accelerated; ORR ~70%) · works after BCMA; oral/skin/nail toxicity, fewer infections
BCMA · BVd, ≥2 lines incl PI + IMiD (re-approved Oct 2025; withdrawn 2022 after DREAMM-3) · keratopathy, REMS
blocks.footnote: Sequencing: BCMA loss after BCMA therapy is common — after BCMA CAR-T/bispecific, switch target (GPRC5D) rather than re-using BCMA when possible.

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing, supportive care, emergencies, agent-specific pitfalls

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m² SC d1, 4, 8, 11 + lenalidomide 25 mg d1–14 + dex 20 mg d1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12 (S0777, ×8)
Dara SC 1800 mg weekly c1–2, q2wk c3–6 + V 1.3 d1, 4, 8, 11 + R 25 d1–21 + dex 40 d1–4, 9–12 ×4 → ASCT → ×2 → D-R (dara q4wk)
Bortezomib 1.3 SC weekly d1, 8, 15, 22 + len 15 d1–21 + dex 20 twice weekly
Dara SC 1800 mg: weekly wk 1–8, q2wk wk 9–24, q4wk from wk 25 + len 25 d1–21 + dex 40 weekly (20 if >75)
Isatuximab 10 mg/kg IV weekly ×4, then q2wk; later q4wk + VRd ×4 → Isa-Rd
Carfilzomib 20 → 27 mg/m² d1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 16 (or 56–70 once weekly) + len 25 d1–21 + dex 40 weekly
Carfilzomib 20 → 56 mg/m² d1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 16 + dex 40 weekly + anti-CD38
Pomalidomide 4 mg d1–21 q28d + dex 40 weekly (20 if ≥75) + dara SC or isatuximab 10 mg/kg
Belantamab 2.5 mg/kg IV q3wk + V 1.3 d1, 4, 8, 11 + dex 20 ×8 cycles, then belantamab alone. Eye-toxicity reductions: 1.9 mg/kg q3wk → 1.9 q8wk
Selinexor 100 mg PO once weekly + bortezomib 1.3 SC weekly + dex 20 twice weekly (35-day)
Iberdomide 1 mg d1–21 q28d + dara SC + dex 40 weekly
1800 mg weekly c1–2, q2wk c3–6, then q4wk — stop at 36 mo (39 cycles)
10 mg d1–28 (15 after 3 mo if tolerated); CrCl 30–60 → 5 mg; <30 → 2.5 mg; dialysis 5 mg after HD
Melphalan 200 mg/m² day −2; 140 mg/m² if renal impairment or frail (100–140 on dialysis); oral cryotherapy
0.06 → 0.3 mg/kg step-up, then 1.5 mg/kg weekly; q2wk after ≥CR ≥6 mo. With dara: 1.5 weekly wk 2–8 → 3 mg/kg q2wk wk 9–24 → q4wk
12 mg d1 → 32 mg d4 → 76 mg weekly; q2wk from wk 25 if responding, q4wk from wk 49
0.01 → 0.06 mg/kg → 0.4 mg/kg weekly, or + 0.4 step → 0.8 mg/kg q2wk
5 → 25 → 200 mg (d1, 8, 15), 200 weekly wk 4–13, q2wk from wk 14; q4wk from wk 24 if ≥VGPR
Flu 30 + Cy 300 mg/m² ×3 d. Cilta-cel 0.5–1.0×106 CAR+ cells/kg · ide-cel 300–510×106. Stay near center 2 wk, no driving 2 wk (REMS removed Jun 2025)
blocks.footnote: Lenalidomide renal dosing (induction): CrCl 30–60 → 10 mg daily · <30 → 15 mg q48h · dialysis → 5 mg daily after HD. Bortezomib, daratumumab, carfilzomib, pomalidomide (off HD) need no renal adjustment; bortezomib: reduce for hepatic impairment.

blocks.heading: Supportive care
items: Bone: zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q4wk (q12wk after ~1–2 yr) or denosumab 120 mg SC q4wk for every patient on active therapy (non-inferior, HR 0.98; less renal toxicity 10% vs 17%, more hypocalcemia 17% vs 12%). Denosumab if CrCl <30; don't stop it abruptly (rebound fractures). Zoledronic acid renal dosing: CrCl 50–60 → 3.5 mg · 40–49 → 3.3 · 30–39 → 3.0 · <30 → avoid
ONJ: dental evaluation before starting; avoid extractions on therapy. Calcium + vitamin D for all (not if hypercalcemic)
VTE with any IMiD: aspirin 81–325 mg if ≤1 risk factor; prophylactic LMWH or apixaban 2.5 mg BID / rivaroxaban 10 mg if higher risk (IMPEDE VTE ≥4, prior VTE, high-dose dex, doxorubicin, immobility)

Infection: acyclovir/valacyclovir with PIs, anti-CD38, CAR-T, bispecifics. Levofloxacin 500 mg ×12 wk at diagnosis (TEAMM: fever or death HR 0.66). PJP prophylaxis with bispecifics, CAR-T, high-dose dex

Bispecifics / CAR-T: IVIG 0.4 g/kg q4wk if IgG <400 mg/dL (hypogammaglobulinemia is near-universal with BCMA agents). Vaccinate: inactivated flu, pneumococcal conjugate, COVID, RSV, recombinant zoster; no live vaccines; re-vaccinate after ASCT

blocks.heading: Myeloma emergencies
items: Renal failure / cast nephropathy (very high involved FLC): start a bortezomib-based regimen immediately (e.g. D-VCd / VRd with renal dosing), high-dose dex, hydrate, treat Ca; stop NSAIDs, avoid IV contrast. Plasma exchange and high-cutoff dialysis are not routine (negative trials). Biopsy if albuminuria → AL, MIDD
Hypercalcemia: IV saline, zoledronic acid (or denosumab if renal failure), calcitonin for the first 48 h, steroids + anti-myeloma therapy

Cord compression: dexamethasone 10 mg IV now + MRI whole spine → RT or surgery (instability) · Hyperviscosity (IgA, IgG3): plasmapheresis · Anemia: treat the myeloma; ESA if Hb <10 despite therapy (VTE risk with IMiDs)

blocks.heading: Pitfalls with modern agents
items: Anti-CD38 → blood bank: dara/isa bind CD38 on reagent RBCs → panreactive indirect antiglobulin test for up to 6 mo. Send type & screen + phenotype/genotype before dose 1; lab uses DTT-treated cells (DTT destroys Kell → give K-negative units). ABO typing is unaffected — tell the blood bank
Anti-CD38 → SPEP/IFE: dara (IgGκ) shows up as a small IgG-κ band that mimics residual disease — use a DIRA / mass-spec assay before calling non-CR
CRS / ICANS: step-up dosing, 48-h admission (or monitored outpatient) after step-ups; tocilizumab for grade ≥2 CRS, dex for ICANS; restart step-up if doses are missed
Cilta-cel: delayed movement/neurocognitive toxicity (parkinsonism) weeks–months out, cranial-nerve (VII) palsy; boxed warning for secondary T-cell malignancies (all CAR-T, Apr 2024), MDS/AML
Talquetamab: dysgeusia, dry mouth, dysphagia, weight loss, skin peeling, nail loss — common and dose-limiting; dose spacing helps
Belantamab: corneal keratopathy (ocular AEs 79–89% in DREAMM-7/8) — blurred vision, dry eye; eye exam at baseline and before doses; hold/delay by exam findings; REMS

blocks.heading: Other agents — when and when not
items: Venetoclax: t(11;14) only, off-label. BELLINI (Vd ± ven): PFS gain but excess deaths (infections), driven by non-t(11;14) — never outside t(11;14)
Selinexor (XPO1): SVd weekly — thrombocytopenia 39% grade 3–4, nausea, hyponatremia, fatigue; give with 5-HT3 + olanzapine prophylaxis
Carfilzomib: HTN, HF, cardiac events — baseline echo and BP control; prefer bortezomib if significant cardiac disease
